report.title: City of Mountain View 2025 Water Quality Report (Consumer Confidence Report, June 2026)

sources_described: The City purchases approximately 90 percent of its drinking water from the San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC) Regional Water System, mostly Sierra Nevada snowmelt stored in Hetch Hetchy Reservoir plus runoff from Alameda, San Mateo and Santa Clara county watersheds; approximately 8 percent is treated surface water purchased from Valley Water (Rinconada Water Treatment Plant; South Bay Aqueduct, Dyer Reservoir, Lake Del Valle, San Luis Reservoir and Calero Reservoir); two percent comes from City-owned groundwater wells in the lower aquifer of the Santa Clara subbasin, blended with SFPUC water and also serving as emergency backup.

extraction_notes: Report covers January-December 2025; states 'In 2025, Mountain View's drinking water met all Federal and State standards' and has no violations section. All data tables are on PDF page 5, which is a two-page spread (printed pages 5 and 6). The source-water table ('CITY OF MOUNTAIN VIEW SOURCE WATER QUALITY DATA FOR 2025') has three source column groups: 'SFPUC' (Range + 'Avg. or [Max]'), 'Valley Water' (Range + 'Avg. or [Max]') and 'CMV Wells' (Range only, footnote 2); one entry per analyte per column, named in source_group. Cells printed '-' (Non Applicable / not reported for that source) were skipped rather than given empty entries; e.g. Barium has CMV Wells data only, Gross Alpha/Uranium have Valley Water and (gross alpha) CMV Wells only, Chlorate SFPUC only. A separate 'MOUNTAIN VIEW DRINKING WATER (1)' table (distribution system: turbidity, TTHMs, HAA-5s, fluoride, total chlorine, free ammonia, customer-tap lead and copper) has a single 'Range or [Avg]' column; source_group = 'Mountain View Drinking Water (distribution system)'. Values printed in square brackets are maxima or averages per the column header ('[Max]'/'[Avg]'). Range lows printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as 0 with the printed form kept in notes; averages printed 'ND' or '<x' are stored as null with range high used as value and detected=true because the range shows a detection. Bracketed MCL column entries ('[1000]', '[800]', '[50]', '[15]', '[1.3]') are notification levels or action levels as printed; 'NS' = No Standard. The report prints a DLR column; numeric DLRs are kept in notes. Sample year is 2025 per the table title except Valley Water radionuclides (footnote 10: last tested 2022) and the CMV Wells gross alpha (year not printed). No PFAS table row exists; the page-4 statement (no PFAS detected, most recent test 2023) is recorded as a flagged text-only entry. The HAA-5 running-annual-average range high (63.0 ppb) is printed above the 60 ppb MCL while footnote (1) says all results met standards; recorded as printed.
